# Build and flash

You need ESP-IDF 5.5 and an ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 with the N16R8 module (16 MB flash, 8 MB octal PSRAM).

## Build and flash

1. Load the ESP-IDF environment in your shell.

   **Load ESP-IDF**

   ```sh
   . ~/esp/esp-idf/export.sh
   ```

2. Set the target and build.

   **Build**

   ```sh
   idf.py set-target esp32s3
   idf.py build
   ```

3. Plug in the board and flash it. Use the port that your system shows for the board.

   **Flash**

   ```sh
   idf.py -p /dev/ttyACM0 flash monitor
   ```

The monitor prints `MDA video running: 720x350, pclk 16257000 Hz, mode 3` when the video driver has started. The default mode joins Wi-Fi and shows frames that you send. Set the network first. See [Send frames over Wi-Fi](../guides/send-frames-over-wifi.md). For a demo that needs no network, see [Choose a demo](../guides/choose-a-demo.md).

> [!NOTE]
> The DevKitC-1 has two USB ports. The port wired to the UART bridge carries the console log. Flashing worked through that port, and it showed up as `/dev/ttyACM0` on Linux.

## Check the sync before you connect video

Wire the sync lines and ground first, as described in [Wire the monitor](../guides/wire-the-monitor.md). Leave the video wire unplugged and power the monitor. You should see a steady raster with no whine from the monitor. Connect the video wire once the monitor holds lock.
